reasoning: Recent data for South Dakota is almost entirely about the 2026 Senate race; there is effectively no fresh presidential polling in the last 45 days, and national forecasters treat the presidential race as safely Republican with no quantified new margin. The best current quantified indicator is the PollsMax aggregate of the now-defunct Beaudion–Rounds contest, showing Republicans ahead by about 24 points statewide, which is consistent with South Dakota’s R+16 Cook PVI and other contextual evidence that the GOP holds a very large advantage. Given the Democratic nominee’s withdrawal and the state’s strong Republican lean, the practical current margin for the Senate race is on the order of **R+20–25**, and for the presidential race at least **R+15–20**, both strongly favoring Republicans overall.

sources.name: PollsMax
sources.details: PollsMax’s 2026 South Dakota Senate polling average between Democrat Julian Beaudion and Republican Sen. Mike Rounds shows Rounds leading 54.9% to 30.7%, an R+24.1 margin statewide.

sources.name: Townhall (reporting on Senate poll)
sources.details: A reported head-to-head poll between incumbent GOP Sen. Mike Rounds and independent Brian Bengs finds Rounds ahead 56% to 33%, an R+23 margin in the Senate race.

sources.name: Politico
sources.details: Politico reports that Democratic Senate nominee Julian Beaudion has ended his campaign, clearing the way for independent Brian Bengs to face Republican Sen. Mike Rounds, underscoring GOP structural strength in the South Dakota Senate race.

sources.name: NBC News
sources.details: NBC News covers Beaudion’s exit and the resulting independent-versus-incumbent general election, treating the South Dakota Senate seat as strongly favorable to Republicans; no new public poll numbers are provided but the context supports a large GOP advantage.

sources.name: Cook Political Report PVI (South Dakota statewide)
sources.details: Cook Political Report’s statewide Partisan Voting Index rates South Dakota as R+16, indicating that in recent presidential elections the state has voted about 16 points more Republican than the national average, which structurally benefits GOP candidates in both presidential and Senate contests.
